seoTitle: How to Start and Join a Zoom Call From Slack
metaDescription: Launch instant Zoom meetings directly from Slack channels using the /zoom slash command after installing the official Zoom app.
intro: Copying a Zoom link into a channel, waiting for everyone to notice it, and then losing the thread once the call starts is the exact friction the Zoom app for Slack removes. Once it's installed, starting a meeting is a single slash command typed into the channel you're already in, and joining is a click on the card it generates — no separate app switch, no hunting for the right link. This guide covers finding the Zoom app in Slack's marketplace, what authorizing it actually involves, and how the day-to-day slash command works once it's connected.

steps.heading: Open the Slack Marketplace to find Zoom
steps.body: Slack's app ecosystem now runs through a full marketplace site rather than just the in-app Apps panel — reachable from the same Tools menu, or directly if a teammate shares a listing link. The marketplace homepage leads with featured and AI-focused apps, but a plain search for "Zoom" in the search bar at the top surfaces the official listing directly, the same way you'd search for any other integration.

image.caption: Slack's Marketplace homepage, where searching by app name is how you find the official Zoom listing among the featured apps.

steps.heading: Install the official Zoom app
steps.body: Open the verified Zoom listing and click Add to Slack. Slack shows you the specific permissions the app is requesting before anything is finalized — typically the ability to post messages, create meeting links, and read basic channel information — and you'll need to click Allow to move forward. Skimming this screen matters more than it seems, since it's the only place you'll see exactly what access you're granting before the integration goes live.

steps.heading: Sign in to your Zoom account
steps.body: After approving the permissions, Slack redirects you to Zoom's own login page to connect your account. Use your organization's Zoom credentials here, then accept the security consent screen that follows — this is the step that actually links your specific Zoom license to your Slack workspace, so the meetings you generate later are tied to your account's settings and plan limits.

steps.heading: Launch a call with the /zoom slash command
steps.body: Back in Slack, go to any channel or direct message, type /zoom, and press Enter. This instantly posts a meeting card with a Join button, generated fresh for that moment rather than reusing a static personal meeting link — useful for keeping unrelated calls from colliding. Anyone in the channel can click Join straight from the card without needing to open Zoom separately first.

steps.heading: Set Zoom as your default call trigger
steps.body: If your team leans on Zoom more than Slack's built-in Huddles, workspace settings let you map the phone or video call icon at the top of a channel to launch Zoom automatically instead of prompting you to choose every time. This is a small setting but it removes a click from the most common action in a fast-moving channel, and it's worth doing once your team has settled on Zoom as the default rather than an occasional alternative.

faq.question: Do all participants need a Zoom account to join?
faq.answer: No, teammates can join through the generated link without needing their own Zoom account, though hosting and admin features vary by role and license.

faq.question: Can I set Zoom as my default call option in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, workspace settings let you map the phone or video icon so it automatically launches Zoom instead of prompting you to pick a tool each time.

faq.question: Does the integration work in direct messages too?
faq.answer: Yes, the /zoom command works the same way in both public channels and direct messages.

faq.question: What happens if my Zoom license doesn't support the meeting length?
faq.answer: The meeting follows whatever limits your connected Zoom account's plan has, so check your subscription if calls are cutting off earlier than expected.

faq.question: Where do I find the Zoom app if it's not in my sidebar shortcuts?
faq.answer: Search for it directly in the Slack Marketplace or the in-app Apps panel under the Tools menu — it doesn't need to be pinned to a shortcut to be installed or used.
